survey_growth_note: Monthly close-approach counts from the JPL catalog include approaches that happened before an object was discovered. As surveys improve, those past approaches are added, so the historical counts rise with the catalog. The known-at-the-time series keeps only objects whose first observation is on or before the approach, and the per-1,000-known-NEO rate divides by the NEO catalog size at the start of the month. Both controls still depend on which objects the surveys find. H < 22 (about 140 m and larger) is less incomplete in recent years and is not a complete record back to 1900. Future months in the CAD feed are predicted approaches of objects known today; they do not include objects nobody has found yet.
